options.content:
DNS VIP `172.53.53.53` → DNSdist on dns-1/2/3 → local BIND for local zones, cluster BIND for hosted zones, Blocky for trusted clients, or Cloudflare DoT for unfiltered clients.

Blocky uses parallel DoT upstreams (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9); its exported metrics do not expose individual upstream health. DNSdist backend checks are lazy. VIP probes originate inside Kubernetes and do not test every client VLAN or the filtered client path. Local BIND and VIP routing state have logs and backend checks, not dedicated metrics. Missing telemetry is unknown.

Upstream classes correspond to DNSdist pools: internal BIND (`bind`), cluster BIND (`k8s`), Blocky (`blocky`), and public Cloudflare resolvers (`cloudflare`). Class health uses the least healthy node, so a fault on one node is not averaged away. Click a class to inspect its backend members; Blocky’s own resolver choices remain on the Blocky dashboard.
